ragSettings.intro: The AI can look things up in your own notes. When you ask a question it first searches the documents in the folders ticked below, answers from what it finds there, and tells you which files the answer came from.

explainer.title: What is the knowledge base?
explainer.whatTitle: What do I get out of it?
explainer.whatBody: You can ask the AI about things written down somewhere in your notes — even when that file is not open at all. For example: “What did I agree with client A about the delivery date?” The AI searches your notes, answers from what is written there, and lists the files it took that from underneath. Clicking one takes you straight there.
explainer.howBody: ScribeDog searches your documents for the words in your question and gives the AI the most fitting passages to read. The search itself runs entirely on your device — nothing is prepared, uploaded or stored permanently. Your notes stay unchanged; they are only read.
explainer.dataBody: Only the passages found for your question go to the AI — not your entire folder. Where they go depends on what you set under “AI settings”: with a service on your own device (such as Ollama) nothing leaves the computer. With a provider on the internet, the passages found are transmitted there. None of this happens unless you switch the knowledge base on — and nothing is ever sent to ScribeDog itself.
explainer.undoBody: Just switch the toggle above off. The AI can then immediately only see the document you have open. You can also exclude individual folders permanently by unticking them — private folders stay out that way while the rest remains searchable. Your notes themselves are never changed or deleted by any of this.
explainer.howBodySemantic: ScribeDog splits your notes into passages and has a kind of summary computed for each one, which makes it possible to search by meaning rather than only by exact words (the technical term is embeddings). Those summaries sit in a file in the .scribedog folder inside your own folder. The words of your question are searched for as well, and both results are merged.
explainer.dataBodySemantic: To prepare them, all files in the ticked folders are sent in full to the service you configured for the knowledge base; after that, only changed files are. When answering, the passages found are also sent to the AI. With a service on your own device (such as Ollama) nothing leaves the computer; with a provider on the internet it does. None of this happens unless you switch the knowledge base on — and nothing is ever sent to ScribeDog itself, not for training either.
explainer.undoBodySemantic: Switch the toggle above off and the AI immediately sees nothing but the open document. "Delete stored data" also removes the prepared file; it sits in the .scribedog folder inside your own folder, and deleting that folder removes all of it. Your notes themselves are never changed or deleted.

mode.title: How the search works
mode.keywordHint: Finds passages that actually contain the words from your question. Needs no preparation and no extra connection — the search runs entirely on your device.
mode.semanticHint: Also finds the right passage when you word your question differently than your note. Your notes have to be prepared once for this: they are read in full and sent to a service you configure below. Words are still searched for as well.
